---
title: SSH
order: 1
---

SSH (Secure Shell) is the way to connect to the clusters. It gives you a
terminal on a remote machine, the *login node*, from where you manage files,
edit code and submit jobs, and it is also what file transfers and editors such
as VS Code use under the hood. This page covers what is common to BioCloud and
AI Cloud; the cluster documentation covers the same ground for each cluster
separately, but describes the setup in slightly different ways.

The login node is shared by everyone using the cluster and is only meant for
light work. Anything that takes more than a few seconds of computation should
be submitted as a job to a compute node instead.

## Hostnames and usernames

| Cluster   | Login node             |
|-----------|------------------------|
| BioCloud  | `bio-fe01.srv.aau.dk`, `bio-fe02.srv.aau.dk` |
| AI Cloud  | `ai-fe02.srv.aau.dk`   |
| Gateway   | `sshgw.aau.dk`         |

On both clusters the username is the full AAU email address, e.g.
`abc@bio.aau.dk`, and the password is the AAU password. Because the username
itself contains an `@`, a login on the command line looks slightly unusual:

```bash
ssh abc@bio.aau.dk@bio-fe01.srv.aau.dk
```

where everything before the last `@` is the username. The first time you
connect to a machine, SSH asks whether you trust its host key, to which the
answer is `yes`.

Access to a cluster has to be granted before the login works; how that is done
is described on the page for each cluster.

## Connecting from outside campus

The clusters are only reachable from the AAU network. From elsewhere there are
two options:

- **The AAU VPN.** When the VPN is connected, everything on this page works as
  it does on campus.
- **The SSH gateway**, `sshgw.aau.dk`. SSH connects to the gateway first and
  jumps from there to the cluster, which requires no VPN client but asks for
  two-factor authentication at the gateway. On the command line this is done
  with `-J`:

  ```bash
  ssh -J abc@bio.aau.dk@sshgw.aau.dk abc@bio.aau.dk@bio-fe01.srv.aau.dk
  ```

In practice, neither of these commands needs to be typed once the
configuration file below is in place.

## The SSH configuration file

SSH reads the file `~/.ssh/config` on your own machine (on Windows
`C:\Users\<name>\.ssh\config`), in which each cluster can be given a short name
together with the username and other settings. We recommend the following,
with `abc@bio.aau.dk` replaced by your own email address:

```
Host sshgw
    HostName sshgw.aau.dk

Host biocloud
    HostName bio-fe01.srv.aau.dk
    # ProxyJump sshgw

Host aicloud
    HostName ai-fe02.srv.aau.dk
    # ProxyJump sshgw

Host sshgw biocloud aicloud
    User abc@bio.aau.dk
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
    ServerAliveInterval 60
```

Connecting is then just

```bash
ssh biocloud
```

and the same short names work for `scp`, `rsync`, VS Code and `git` remotes.
When working from outside campus without the VPN, remove the `#` in front of
`ProxyJump sshgw` for the cluster in question, such that SSH goes through the
gateway automatically. `ServerAliveInterval` keeps an idle connection from
being dropped.

The configuration deliberately points at one specific BioCloud login node,
`bio-fe01`, rather than switching between the two. Things that live on the
login node, such as a `tmux` session, are only found again when returning to
the same node.

## SSH keys

Typing the password at every login quickly becomes tedious, and tools such as
VS Code and `rsync` connect several times. An SSH key replaces the password: it
consists of a private key, which should never leave your own machine, and a
public key, which needs to be copied to the cluster.

A key is created once for each machine you work from with

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519
```

accepting the default location (`~/.ssh/id_ed25519`). The passphrase it asks
for protects the private key should your laptop be lost, and setting one is
recommended; macOS, Linux and Windows can all remember it after the first use,
such that it does not need to be typed again.

The public key is then copied to a cluster with

```bash
ssh-copy-id biocloud
```

which asks for the AAU password one last time. On Windows, where
`ssh-copy-id` is not available, the following does the same in PowerShell:

```powershell
type $env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub | ssh biocloud "mkdir -p ~/.ssh && cat >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys"
```

Repeat this for `aicloud`. If the login still asks for a password afterwards,
the cause is almost always the permissions on the cluster, which SSH requires
to be strict:

```bash
chmod 700 ~/.ssh && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
```

The same key can be added to GitHub, which is the most convenient way to clone
and push repositories from your own machine. For using GitHub from the
clusters themselves, the BioCloud documentation describes
[how to connect to GitHub](https://docs.biocloud.bio.aau.dk/guides/git/).

## Copying files

Files that are not code, e.g. input structures or results, are copied with
`rsync` or `scp` from your own machine. Code is better moved through git, by
pushing from one machine and pulling on the other, such that the cluster and
your laptop never drift apart.

```bash
# Copy a directory to the cluster
rsync -av results/ biocloud:project/results/

# Copy it back again
rsync -av biocloud:project/results/ results/
```

The trailing `/` on the source matters: with it, the *contents* of `results`
are copied, without it the directory itself is copied into the destination.
`rsync` only transfers what has changed and can resume an interrupted
transfer, which makes it the better choice for anything large. `scp` works the
same way for single files, e.g. `scp structure.traj aicloud:`, and is also
available on Windows, where `rsync` is not installed by default.

## Editors

VS Code with the
[Remote - SSH](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/remote/ssh) extension can
open a folder on the cluster as if it were local, and it picks up the hosts
from the configuration file. It does, however, run a server process on the
login node, and the two clusters take different views on this:

- **BioCloud** supports it, but asks that you open a project folder rather
  than the whole home directory, as indexing the latter runs on the login
  node. BioCloud additionally offers VS Code, Jupyter and RStudio through its
  [web portal](https://docs.biocloud.bio.aau.dk/access/webportal/), where they
  run as a job on a compute node.
- **AI Cloud** discourages Remote - SSH on its front-end node, and likewise
  asks that AI coding assistants are not run there. On AI Cloud, code should
  therefore be edited locally and moved with git.

For small edits directly on the cluster, a terminal editor such as `nano` or
`vim` is sufficient.

## Common problems

`Connection timed out` or no response at all
:   You are not on the AAU network. Connect the VPN, or enable
    `ProxyJump sshgw` in the configuration file.

`Permission denied`
:   Either the username is wrong, which should be the full email address, or
    access to the cluster has not been granted yet.

`WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED`
:   The login node has been reinstalled, which happens occasionally after
    maintenance. If the cluster has announced maintenance, the old key is
    removed with `ssh-keygen -R <hostname>`; if not, ask before connecting.
